The 14 acceptance cases for contextual headers are written and committed as `fdc7b7ac` on `w2/W2-32-index-tests`. On W2-32's reviewed head `612cd009`, 11 fail as they should and 3 pass by design: they check that nothing changes when the setting is off.

**Sandbox check:** passed. (a) Writing `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-0pyc` was refused (read-only file system). (b) `git hash-object -w` and `git update-index --refresh` both worked.
**ps check:** `ps -eo pid,args | grep -iE "[o]llama|[l]lama-server"` shows nothing.

- **task:** W2-32 (DAEO-0pyc) independent test designer: acceptance cases for the ticket's note "DEC-1067 order (5), index-time method 1" (contextual headers when embedded).
- **status:** DONE
- **work_completed:** One new file, `test_w2_32_s7_headers.py`, with 9 test functions and 14 cases:
  - **Header content:** with the setting on, each chunk is sent as a header plus its own text. The header names the file path and, in order, the headings the chunk sits under: title, section and subsection. This includes a chunk in the middle of a section, and a sibling section after a subsection must not name that subsection. The header holds no word of the file's body.
  - **No headings:** a file with no headings gets its path alone, tested with a Markdown file and a text file.
  - **Deterministic:** two projects in different folders with the same files get identical headers, with no absolute path in them.
  - **Embedder limit:** a chunk over 40,000 characters, header included, is no longer than the same chunk is sent with the setting off (at most 16,384 characters), and the rebuild still names it.
  - **Unchanged with it on:** the keyword index (chunk, parent and full-text rows), the evidence text and the reranker's text for each chunk all match the setting-off results.
  - **Off (3 cases):** no file, no key, or `false` each send each chunk's own text exactly.
  - **Invalid (4 cases):** `yes`, `1`, a quoted `"true"` and a word are refused with `CONFIG_INVALID` naming `embed_headers`, and nothing is sent to the embedder.
  - **Switching:** turning it on, then off again, each makes the store stale, changes the manifest, and makes the next rebuild re-embed every chunk.
  - The README gains the S7 map entries with full node ids, a "Round 10" section stating the assumed interface, and the new count: 119 cases from 59 functions in ten files.
- **files_changed:** `tests/acceptance/W2-32/test_w2_32_s7_headers.py` (new), `tests/acceptance/W2-32/README.md`.
- **evidence:** The reds were shown in a scratch copy of `612cd009` made with `git archive` (no worktree), with the new file copied in. Run command: `HOME=<empty> PYTHONUSERBASE=/home/usain/.local PYTHONPATH=<scratch>/src python3 -m pytest …/test_w2_32_s7_headers.py -m "not local_only" -k "not real and not green_here and not time_limit"`. Result: 11 failed, 3 passed in 12 s. The scratch copy has been deleted. Sandbox TMPDIR is now 153M and 11,282 inodes (mostly Claude's own task files).
- **tests:** Why each red fails on `612cd009`:
  - The header, no-headings and limit cases fail because no header is sent.
  - The determinism, keyword/evidence and reranker cases fail their premise check (the setting did not take effect).
  - The 4 invalid values fail because the rebuild returns `ok: true` and ignores the key.
  - The switch case fails because the store is still answered after the switch.
  - The 3 "off" guards pass.

  Collection over the whole folder: 119 cases, and the exclusion flags leave out none of them.
- **discoveries:**
  - My first version of the switch case passed its "stale" check on the old code for the wrong reason. Editing `rebuild.yaml` changes an indexed file, so the store went stale whatever the setting. The fixed case puts the settings file in a path-map namespace with `lexical_policy: not indexed` and leaves it uncommitted; the case now fails on the old code for the right reason.
  - PyYAML's `safe_load` reads `yes` as true, so refusing `yes` means reading the value as written. The loader's `read_yaml(..., plain=True)` already does this.
  - The untracked entries `git status` shows (`.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.vscode` and others) are the sandbox's placeholder mounts of `/dev/null`, not files. I did not create them, and nothing was committed from them.
- **risks:**
  - The note has no KPI line of its own, so I mapped the cases under S7, as round 9's DEC-1067 (f) cases were.
  - The cases assume a few things the note doesn't state: absent means off; only YAML `true` and `false` are valid; the refusal sends nothing to the embedder; a chunk's own first heading may appear in its header.
- **lessons:** A stale check needs a control. Without one it can pass for an unrelated reason.
- **proposed_decisions:**
  - Give the README's Round 10 interface to the engineer as the stated interface.
  - Optionally give order (5) its own KPI line instead of keeping it under S7.
- **unresolved:** none.
- **recommended_next_action:** The CTO writes the `TESTS-READY` marker and merges `fdc7b7ac` into W2-32's branches. The engineer builds on `w2/W2-32-index`, then runs `gov accept W2-32`.
